answers.answer: M1’s SchedulerCore._assign reads READY tasks without resource conflicts and available capacity, then calls AssignmentPort.propose outside a transaction. Each proposal goes through claim in a separate write transaction, rechecking readiness, capacity, live attempts and conflicts. That transaction creates the RESERVED attempt and fencing token, makes the task ACTIVE, stores holds and adds the start outbox item. SqliteRepository commits state and audit together. Dispatcher separately commits the delivery counter before calling execution.start, then records its acknowledgement in another transaction. CoreExecutionPort supplies the approved task’s repository and plan hash. M3 validates the request, resolves its route and checks its workspace before Ledger.insert atomically records QUEUED. M3 acceptance acknowledges durable admission; process launch occurs later through _schedule and _launch.

M1 startup checks the persisted plan binding and reconciles live attempts. A RESERVED pending start with zero deliveries is skipped; a possibly delivered start is queried. M3’s queued/preparing/settling statuses map to M1 running, so an accepted order need not already have launched to prevent resend. Running/finished observations mark the start delivered; unknown preserves uncertainty. Delivery retries also query whenever the previous delivery counter is nonzero and resend only after not_found leaves the attempt RESERVED with a pending start. M3 first checks by idempotency key: matching requests return duplicate, differing requests return KEY_CONFLICT. Ledger.insert repeats that check atomically and rejects an existing attempt ID under another key.

Lease expiry only sets needs_reconcile. For a live attempt outside the VERIFYING exception, unknown clears that flag, schedules another observation after min(lease_seconds, reconcile_seconds), and changes the attempt to UNCERTAIN. The task remains ACTIVE and its resource holds remain: this branch never calls end_attempt or release. It cannot be claimed again because claim requires READY, and recovery proposals are requested only for RECOVERING tasks. Thus lease expiry plus unknown does not authorize a replacement attempt.

not_found permits redelivery only when the start outbox item is pending and the current attempt is RESERVED or UNCERTAIN; UNCERTAIN is restored to RESERVED. Dispatcher then verifies it is still RESERVED with a pending start before resending. A genuinely never-attempted start skips startup querying altogether. After recorded delivery, or outside those permitted states, not_found closes the attempt FAILED with cause lost, releases holds and voids pending orders; an ACTIVE task enters RECOVERING, or CANCELLED if cancellation was requested. Normal VERIFYING reconciliation has its separate ignore guard.

M3 classifies completed provider output with returncode zero as FINISHED; zero exit alone is insufficient, and partial output becomes FAILED. report.json claims are merely attached to the outcome. Settlement preserves the handoff and atomically records the terminal state/event; preservation failure can downgrade FINISHED to FAILED. AgentExecutor._deliver forwards the persisted execution_finished through CoreEventSink to SchedulerCore.ingest. apply_event advances the attempt to VERIFYING and creates a verification order carrying approved criteria/checks; the task stays ACTIVE. Only apply_verdict can accept the attempt, release holds and complete the task. It requires VERIFYING, a named verifier and nonempty acceptance evidence; independence defaults on but checks label inequality and can be disabled.

No. For VERIFYING, ordinary observations failed, not_found, cancelled and unknown are audited as observation_ignored and return before changing the attempt or lease. The explicit exception is manual=True. operations.resolve_attempt requires a nonempty operator name, a live attempt and an allowed outcome, audits the action, then calls apply_observation with manual=True. An operator may therefore fail/cancel it or request verification again via finished; this does not directly accept work.

Preflight checks plan/revision first: mismatch is invalid/wrong_plan. Remembered IDs return duplicate before attempt/token checks. Unknown attempts or task mismatches are invalid/unknown_attempt; a supplied wrong token is stale/token_mismatch; ordinary events for an older attempt are stale/superseded_attempt. Ordinary terminal-attempt events are stale/attempt_closed. Only applied messages are remembered; rejected IDs remain correctable, and heartbeats return noop without being remembered. Ordinary ID memory is bounded. incident_observed deliberately allows known superseded and terminal attempts, while retaining plan/task/token checks. It audits and remembers the incident before lifecycle or lease updates, so it cannot change execution state. Incident deduplication additionally consults persisted audit keys, surviving ordinary-ID eviction.

Cancellation before any delivery attempt—RESERVED, pending start, deliveries==0—immediately ends the attempt CANCELLED, voids its orders and releases holds. A pending start with a positive delivery count may already have reached M3: cancellation instead voids the start and adds a cancel order, retaining the live attempt and holds. The same applies to already dispatched/running work. A cancel acknowledgement merely flags reconciliation; confirmed cancellation/failure closes and releases. Dispatcher also prevents pending starts from being sent once cancellation is requested. VERIFYING’s observation guard still applies.

AgentExecutor construction invokes _recover before its loop starts. RUNNING rows are watched: exit.json triggers settlement; otherwise recorded shim PID/incarnation is checked, then exit.json is reread after apparent death; absent results become lost settlement. PREPARING recovery reads shim.json and exit.json, checks shim and child identities, and searches shim argv when neither file exists. It aborts/waits for an unidentified shim, adopts recorded live/result-bearing work, or settles an exit without shim metadata. Only after finding no running work does it prepare again, sweeping an exclusive persisted workspace first. SETTLING resumes from its persisted outcome and preserves work before terminal publication. IdentityUnknown conservatively counts as alive, so unreadable process identity does not justify another launch. These facts establish local supervision status, not remote provider effects.

wire connects the approved plan, CoreExecutionPort and RouteResolver, optionally constructing the M2 ledger lookup. CoreExecutionPort validates plan/revision and task, then adds the approved plan hash. M2 resolution accepts only the persisted selected route, returning its plan/revision/hash/task and any later superseding decision. RouteResolver rejects missing references, context/hash mismatch, supersession and expired quota evidence. validate_route checks provider/model/profile policy and compares a supplied account_ref with the current account reference when available; MethodologyDriver.prepare repeats validation and builds the profile environment. Single-use route references are reserved atomically in M3’s ledger. There is no silent fallback from an invalid opaque reference to a direct route; direct routing is a separate explicitly allowed path. Custom resolver injection is possible, and m2_account_ref returns empty if M2 cannot import.

Source assertions, not executed results: CrashPoints.test_crash_after_the_executor_took_the_order_never_starts_a_second_writer simulates acceptance followed by crash and asserts one start, one executor record and recovered RUNNING. test_crash_after_delivery_but_before_the_ack_was_recorded explicitly restores pending/RESERVED and asserts no additional start after restart. PortFailures’ unavailable-query test asserts UNCERTAIN, one retained hold and refusal to reclaim. Idempotency’s duplicate-event test asserts unchanged snapshot and audit length. Stale’s old-attempt test asserts lifecycle events cannot change tasks or holds. VerifyingIsSettledByVerdict’s unknown-observation test asserts VERIFYING survives expired-lease queries and a subsequent verdict completes. Incident tests separately assert superseded incidents only audit and deduplication survives eviction/restart.

The source implements durable local admission, same-key replay protection, reconciliation and verdict-gated completion. It does not establish exactly-once effects at arbitrary external providers: provider processes launch outside ledger transactions, and process loss can leave remote effects unknown. Neither clean exit nor a success claim automatically accepts quality. M6 verification is wired only when quality_store_path is supplied; otherwise verification is caller-provided or absent. Core independence is configurable label comparison, not authenticated proof of reviewer identity or substantive correctness. Profile authorization, executable checks and fresh quota evidence are launch gates, not proof of live-account availability. No tests or live checks were run.

unknowns: Actual remote provider effects after interruption, current account credentials/quota/availability, deployed port configuration and substantive work quality cannot be established from this snapshot.
The cited tests were read as source assertions only; no execution or passing result is claimed.
